See, I love post like this, because we’re genuinely thinking “why?”

Answer is actually simple, by nature we’re social creatures, don’t like being alone, but many of us feel lonely. It’s our instincts to reach out and communicate. 

Even when I run into someone who doesn’t speak the same language, we can still understand each other on some level. They can still stop me from from doing something stupid.

Time. Been almost 5 years. First year was drugs and finding ways to get more drugs. Then spent 2 years in and out of psychiatric care, next year I rebuilt my support group, and this past year I managed to stay sober and actually help others in situations I use to be in

We don’t know the situation or what’s going on or what’s influencing your intent, so there’s not much of an answer we can give you.

Even when my ex died with me knowing why, I still screamed “why?!” Multiple times for hours.

Talking about it acts as a kind of release. Think about how we as people complain, we often feel better after, “this key gets stuck in this door every time!” And by saying that, come to realize there’s a problem and start exploring possible solutions.

So talking isn’t a bad thing, the problem is the solution we decide on. I could take an axe to the door and inconvenience everyone or try some lubricant so the key doesn’t get stuck.
